characters.robot: giant old armoured robot with rust, moss and a round chest light, in a forest

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: This robot isn't from a video AI. No camera, no stock footage. Every frame was painted into my Paint app, one stroke at a time. Let me show you the crew that made it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: First, the writer. I type one sentence. A giant robot has knelt in a forest so long that moss grows over it. That's it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Next, the set builder. That's Claude Opus, an AI. It doesn't draw a picture. It builds the whole world out of shapes, like a model kit. The armor, the trees, the ground. Here's what that looks like before any color.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then it paints the props. Rust on the metal, moss on the shoulders, bark on the trees.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then the lighting crew. That's Blender, free software that works out how real sunlight bounces through mist and off metal. That's why it looks real. Nobody painted those shadows. The light made them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then my painter, MattPaint. It takes each frame and paints it, line by line, like a printer. Almost six hundred thousand strokes for one picture. A hundred and twenty pictures for ten seconds.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then the composer. Song Forge, my music maker, wrote the score. And the voice you're hearing right now? That's a copy of my voice, made on my own computer.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And the editor, Story Forge, puts it all together.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The first try took four and a half hours and looked like a pile of blocks. Now it's seven minutes. I looked for anyone else painting movies this way. I couldn't find one.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Everything runs on my laptop except the set builder. It's all free on GitHub. Now watch the robot wake up.
